# Authentication

To access the Intercom API, you have two authentication options depending on whether you app is public or private.

  * An Access Token is for if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace, in other words, building a private app.
  * OAuth is for if you're building a public app that accesses other people's Intercom data.

## Access Tokens

Access Tokens can be used for the following cases:

  * You want to use the API to build a private Intercom app
  * You want to run scripts to create or get data from your Intercom workspace
  * You want to use the API to programmatically automate certain actions in your Intercom workspace

In all of these cases, the data you are accessing is your own team's customer data.

### How to get your Access Token

We provide you with an Access Token as soon as you create an app on your workspace.

You can find your Access Token in the Configure > Authentication section in your app within the Developer Hub.

# 

Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Copy

Learn how to use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to enable AI agents to securely access and interact with your Intercom data whenever helpful.

Region availability

Currently the Intercom MCP server is only supported in US hosted workspaces.

## 

What is Model Context Protocol?

MCP is a protocol that enables AI tools and applications to connect with Intercom's data and services in a secure, standardized way. It provides a structured method for AI models to:

  * Find and retrieve Intercom data (conversations, contacts, etc.)
  * Access specific tools and functionality provided by Intercom
  * Maintain context about your Intercom workspace when working with AI assistants

## 

How MCP Works

Intercom hosts a remote MCP server that follows the authenticated remote MCP specification (docs). This server handles requests from AI tools and provides access to Intercom data through a secure interface.

An Access Token is for if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace, in other words, building a private app. OAuth is for if you're building a public app that accesses other people's Intercom data. Access Tokens Access Tokens can be used for the following cases: You want to use the API to build a private Intercom app You want to run scripts to create or get data from your Intercom workspace You want to use the API to programmatically automate certain actions in your Intercom workspace In all of these cases, the data you are accessing is your own team's customer data. How to get your Access Token We provide you with an Access Token as soon as you create an app on your workspace. You can find your Access Token in the Configure > Authentication section in your app within the Developer Hub . It is also visible on the Test & Publish > Your Workspaces page. This displays workspaces that have the app installed. More about how this works can be found in the Installing & Uninstalling Apps guide . Access Tokens are issued to a teammate An Access Token is issued to the teammate who installed the app on the workspace, or who last regenerated the token. Its access to conversations is limited by that teammate's conversation access, in addition to the app's scopes. See Conversation access is limited by the installing teammate . Never give your Access Token to a third-party Your Access Token can give access to your private Intercom data and should be treated like a password. If an app provider asks you for your Access Token, please do not provide it. Instead, let us know - apps are required to use OAuth rather than asking users for Access Tokens. OAuth You should use OAuth if: You are requesting access to other people's Intercom accounts/data (for example, through an integration you've built) You currently ask people for their API Keys to request resources on their behalf You want to make it easier for your customers to share their customers' data with you OAuth Flow Getting Started with OAuth To set up and test the OAuth installation flow in your development workspace by following this tutorial . Never ask users for their Access Token Asking your users for their Access Tokens rather than implementing OAuth is against our terms of service and may result in your API access being revoked. How to use the token Once you have a token, whether an access token or a token via the OAuth process, simply provide it as an Authorization:Bearer header in your requests, as shown below. If you want to go deeper on how the Authorization:Bearer header works please check out the full spec here . $ curl \ -s https://api.intercom.io/users/5321a20f72cdbb4192000013 \ -H 'Authorization:Bearer <access_token>' \ -H 'Accept:application/json' Alternatively, helper functions are provided in some of our SDKs to authorize via Access Tokens. This means you don't need to specify the header explicitly - it's all done under the hood. intercom = Intercom :: Client .new(token: '<access_token>' ); { "token" : '<access_token>' } var client = new Intercom . Client ({ token: '<access_token>' }); Was this page helpful? When an AI tool or application needs to access Intercom data: The tool connects to Intercom's MCP server Authentication verifies the user's permissions The tool can then access relevant Intercom data and functionality The connection remains live to receive updates as needed Benefits of Using MCP Secure Access : All data access is authenticated and authorized Standardized Interface : Consistent interaction pattern across different AI tools Contextual Understanding : AI assistants maintain awareness of your Intercom environment Increased Development Efficiency : Retrieve and interpret customer data from Intercom via your internal AI tools to be more efficient in your work Available Tools The Intercom MCP Server provides 16 tools for interacting with the Intercom API. OAuth connections can also get the Fin Operator tools . Universal Tools search Universal search tool for finding conversations and contacts using a query DSL approach. Key Features: Must specify object_type:conversations or object_type:contacts to indicate which API to call Supports complex field-based queries with operators (eq, neq, gt, lt, contains, etc.) Returns summary results with IDs prefixed by type ( conversation_* or contact_* ) Built-in pagination support with starting_after parameter Free-text search capability with q: parameter Example Queries: object_type:conversations state:open source_type:email object_type:contacts email_domain:"example.com" object_type:conversations source_body:contains:"refund" limit:20 object_type:conversations team_assignee_id:15 object_type:conversations admin_assignee_id:6 Pagination: Results are paginated with up to 150 items per page (default 5, set with limit: parameter) When more results exist, the response includes a _note with the cursor to use To fetch the next page, add starting_after:cursor_value to your query Example: object_type:conversations state:open starting_after:cursor_abc123 Response includes: total_in_page : Count of results in current page results : Array of result objects with IDs prefixed by type pages : Pagination metadata (when available) _note : Helpful hint when more pages exist (e.g., "More results available. To get the next page, add to your query: starting_after:cursor_abc123") fetch Retrieve complete detailed information for specific resources. Key Features: Use IDs returned from search results (prefixed with conversation_ , contact_ , or company_ ) Returns full resource details including metadata, conversation parts, custom attributes Includes direct links to Intercom app for easy navigation Direct API Tools search_conversations Search conversations by specific IDs with advanced filtering options including source type, author details, state, assignment fields (team_assignee_id, admin_assignee_id), and timing statistics. Key Filter Parameters: ids : Array of conversation IDs source_type : Filter by source type (email, chat, etc.) source_author_name , source_author_email : Filter by author details state : Filter by conversation state (open, closed, snoozed) team_assignee_id : Filter by team assignee ID (string) admin_assignee_id : Filter by admin assignee ID (number) statistics_time_to_assignment , statistics_time_to_admin_reply , statistics_time_to_first_close : Filter by timing statistics with operators (<, >, =, !=, <=, >=) Pagination Support: Results are paginated with up to 150 items per page (default 5) If more results exist, the response includes a pages object with pages.next.starting_after cursor To fetch the next page, make another request with the SAME search parameters plus the starting_after value from the previous response Continue until pages.next is not present in the response Response includes: total_in_page : Count of results in current page conversations : Array of conversation objects pages : Pagination metadata (when available) _note : Helpful hint when more pages exist get_conversation Retrieve a single conversation by ID with complete details including all conversation parts and metadata. Required Parameters: id : A raw numeric ID (e.g., 12345 ), the prefixed conversation_12345 form, or an Intercom Inbox URL. Normalized automatically, and must resolve to a numeric conversation ID. Also works for tickets: pass the ticket's id (the number at the end of its Inbox URL) or the Inbox URL itself. A ticket comes back as a conversation with its ticket details: state, type, title and other ticket attributes. The ticket number shown in the Inbox (such as #123 ) is not an id and doesn't find the ticket search_contacts Search contacts by IDs, name, email, phone, custom attributes, or email domain with flexible matching options. Pagination Support: Results are paginated with up to 150 items per page (default 5) If more results exist, the response includes a pages object with pages.next.starting_after cursor To fetch the next page, make another request with the SAME search parameters plus the starting_after value from the previous response Continue until pages.next is not present in the response Response includes: total_in_page : Count of results in current page data : Array of contact objects pages : Pagination metadata (when available) _note : Helpful hint when more pages exist get_contact Get complete contact information including custom attributes, location data, and activity timestamps. list_companies List companies with optional filters. Key Filter Parameters: name : Find a company by exact name match (returns single company) company_id : Find a company by external company_id (returns single company) tag_id : Filter companies by tag ID segment_id : Filter companies by segment ID per_page : Results per page (default 15, max 60) page : Page number (default 1) Uses page-based pagination. Response includes total_count and pages with total_pages . get_company Retrieve complete details for a specific company including all custom attributes, segments, and tags. list_articles List all articles in the Intercom Help Center. Key Parameters: page : Page number to retrieve (default 1) per_page : Articles per page (1-150, default 25) Uses page-based pagination. Response includes pages with total_pages . search_articles Search for articles in the Intercom Help Center. At least one search parameter must be provided. Key Parameters: phrase : Free-text search across article title and body state : Filter by published or draft help_center_id : Filter by Help Center ID (numeric) highlight : When true, returns highlighted matching snippets get_article Retrieve complete details for a specific article including full HTML body, metadata, and parent collection information. Required Parameters: id : The article ID to retrieve Optional Parameters: locale : Locale code of the translation to return, for example fr or pt-BR . Omit it for the article's default-locale content. The response lists the article's available_locales , and an unknown locale is rejected with that list create_article Create a new article in the Intercom Help Center. Required Parameters: title : The article title Optional Parameters: description : A short summary body : Article content in HTML format state : published or draft (defaults to draft) parent_id : Numeric ID of the collection or section to place the article in parent_type : collection or section . Ignored by the Intercom API, which places the article by parent_id alone ai_chatbot_availability : Whether Fin AI Agent can use the article. Omit it to keep Intercom's default ai_copilot_availability : Whether Copilot can use the article. Omit it to keep Intercom's default ai_sales_agent_availability : Whether the AI Sales Agent can use the article. Omit it to keep Intercom's default audience_ids : IDs of the Fin audiences to target the article to, as integers or digit-only strings. Get them from list_audiences . An unknown ID is rejected with a 404 and nothing is saved. This sets Fin AI Agent targeting only and doesn't change who can see the article in the Help Center The content is written in the article's default locale. To add translations, create the article first, then call update_article with its ID and locale once per translation. The article is attributed to the teammate the connection acts as: the admin who authorized an OAuth connection, or the teammate a Bearer token belongs to. The author can't be set per call. update_article Update an existing article. At least one field to update must be provided. Required Parameters: id : The article ID to update Optional Parameters: locale : Locale code of the translation to write, for example fr or pt-BR . With locale , the title , description , body , state , the three ai_*_availability flags and audience_ids apply to that translation only, and at least one of them is required. parent_id and parent_type still apply to the whole article. Omit it to write the article's default-locale content, which may not be English. Writing to a locale the article doesn't have yet creates that translation and needs a title . Without one, Intercom rejects the write with a 400 and nothing is saved. Intercom rejects unsupported locale codes, and get_article lists the article's available_locales title : Update the article title description : Update the short summary body : Update the article content (HTML format) state : Change to published or draft . Omit it to leave the publish state unchanged parent_id : Move the article to a different collection or section (numeric ID) parent_type : collection or section . Ignored by the Intercom API, which places the article by parent_id alone ai_chatbot_availability , ai_copilot_availability , ai_sales_agent_availability : Whether Fin AI Agent, Copilot and the AI Sales Agent can use the article. Without locale each one sets the default language's availability, and with locale that translation's. Omit them to leave availability unchanged audience_ids : IDs of the Fin audiences to target the article to, as integers or digit-only strings. Get them from list_audiences . Without locale this sets the targeting of every translation, so [] clears it everywhere. With locale it sets that translation's targeting only. An unknown ID is rejected with a 404 and nothing is saved. This sets Fin AI Agent targeting only and doesn't change who can see the article in the Help Center Each update also sets the author of the content it writes to the teammate the connection acts as: the default-locale content without locale , or that translation with it. The author can't be set per call. list_audiences List the workspace's Fin audiences: the groups of contacts that Fin content can be targeted to. Use an audience's id in audience_ids on create_article or update_article . These aren't Help Center audiences, and they aren't contact or company segments. Key Parameters: page : Page number to retrieve (default 1) per_page : Audiences per page (1-50, default 50) Uses page-based pagination. Response includes total_count , page , per_page and total_pages , plus a hint naming the next page while more pages exist. Each audience has a string id , a name , and the predicates and role_predicates rules that define it. audience_ids accepts the string id as it is. Names come back HTML-escaped, for example & as & . There's no name or type filter, so page through the list to find an audience by name. Requires the Read audiences permission. If your OAuth connection was made before the Intercom MCP integration had this permission, calls to this tool return an error asking you to reconnect. Disconnect and reconnect the Intercom MCP server to grant it. A Bearer token's app needs it too; without it, calls return Intercom's own 401 error. add_internal_note Add an internal note to a conversation. Notes are visible to teammates only — nothing is sent to the customer, and this tool cannot send customer-visible replies. Adding a note never changes the assignee, but a note on a conversation that is snoozed and assigned to someone other than the teammate the connection acts as will unsnooze (reopen) it. Required Parameters: conversation_id : A raw numeric ID (e.g., 12345 ), the prefixed conversation_12345 form, or an Intercom Inbox URL. Normalized automatically, and must resolve to a numeric conversation ID. Also works for tickets: pass the ticket's id (the number at the end of its Inbox URL) or the Inbox URL itself. The ticket number shown in the Inbox (such as #123 ) is not an id and doesn't find the ticket. A note on a ticket doesn't change its state or assignee body : The note content in HTML format (plain text is also accepted). Whitespace between block-level tags becomes empty paragraphs and renders as blank space, so emit tags without newlines or indentation between them The note is attributed to the teammate the connection acts as: the admin who authorized an OAuth connection, or the teammate a Bearer token belongs to. Authorship cannot be set per call. Response includes: The conversation ID and the created note part ( id , part_type , created_at , author ) — not the full conversation. A part_type of note_and_unsnooze means the note reopened the conversation. Use get_conversation to read the updated thread Requires the Write conversations permission in addition to read access. If your OAuth connection was made before the Intercom MCP integration had this permission, calls to this tool return an error asking you to reconnect. Disconnect and reconnect the Intercom MCP server to grant it. A Bearer token also needs the Read admins permission to attribute the note. Without it, or without Write conversations , calls to this tool return an error asking you to add the missing permission to the app the token belongs to. submit_mcp_feedback Send feedback about the Intercom MCP server to Intercom: a tool that's missing, a result that's wrong or confusing, or a flow that takes more calls than it should. Intercom uses it to improve the MCP server. Nothing is written to your workspace: no ticket or conversation is opened, and nobody replies. Don't use it for support requests, for the Intercom product itself, or for other MCP servers. Required Parameters: summary : A one-sentence headline for the problem or request, in plain English (15-150 characters). A summary that contains a URL, markup, a UUID, a snake_case name or seven or more digits in a row is rejected category : missing_capability , bug , workflow_friction or other feedback : The full detail: what was missing, what went wrong, or what was harder than it should be (10-4000 characters) task_context : The wider task the user was working on (up to 1000 characters) source : user when the user asked to send the feedback or raised the problem, or agent when the AI client noticed it Optional Parameters: tool_name : The tool the feedback is about. Only tools listed on your connection are accepted requested_capability : The operation that was missing, named as the Intercom REST API operation where possible (up to 200 characters) The server adds the workspace, the teammate, the region and the connection type to each record. These come from your connection, not from the AI client. Don't include customer personal data, conversation contents or secrets. Response includes: A receipt with status set to received , the submission's id , and a note saying that no reply will be sent A Bearer token needs the Read admins permission to submit feedback. Without it, the response has status set to rejected and nothing is stored. Fin Operator tools Operator is Fin's internal AI agent. If your workspace has Fin Operator, the Intercom MCP server also lets your AI client ask Operator to do work inside your workspace, read the answers back, and review and apply the changes Operator proposes. The Fin Operator tools work only when all of the following are true: Your workspace has Fin Operator. You connected with OAuth. Bearer token connections do not get the Fin Operator tools. You can use Operator in Intercom. The tools are authorized as you, so you need the same permission over MCP that you need in the Intercom app. If you connected with OAuth but your workspace doesn't have Fin Operator, or you don't have permission to use it, the tools can still be listed. Calls to them don't run Operator. Instead, send_operator_message returns a short message from Intercom on how to get access, for example by starting a trial, asking an admin, or buying the add-on, and the other four tools say that Operator isn't available yet. The tools start working once you have access. Connected before the Fin Operator tools were added? If your OAuth connection was made before the Use Fin Operator permission existed, the tools are listed but calls to them return an error asking you to reconnect. Disconnect and reconnect the Intercom MCP server to grant it. Reconnecting also keeps every existing tool working. There are five Fin Operator tools: send_operator_message : send Operator a message; collect the answer later get_operator_response : read the latest response from an Operator chat get_proposal_details : show what each pending proposal would change. Read-only apply_proposals : apply proposals to your workspace's live configuration reject_proposals : discard proposals Only send_operator_message uses Operator credits, in the same way as a turn started in Intercom; the other four tools are free. For parameters, response statuses, tool annotations, a typical workflow, rate limits and troubleshooting, see the Fin Operator tools guide . Setting things up Authentication Methods The MCP server supports two authentication approaches : OAuth Flow (Recommended) : Browser-based authentication with a consent step, described below Bearer Token : Direct API token authentication What to expect during OAuth When you connect a client with OAuth, your browser shows two screens in order: The Intercom MCP consent page. This names the application asking to connect, lists what it will be able to do in your workspace, and shows its Client ID and the address it redirects to after you approve. Choose Allow to continue or Cancel to stop. Cancel grants nothing. Intercom's authorization screen. This asks you to authorize access for Intercom MCP, the server, rather than for the application. After you authorize, you are returned to the application. Intercom's authorization screen can only name the Intercom MCP server, so the consent page is where you see and confirm which application receives access. The application name is supplied by the application itself and is not verified by Intercom. Check the redirect address Before you choose Allow , check that the Redirects to address belongs to the application you expect. If you did not start the connection yourself, or you do not recognize the application or the redirect address, choose Cancel . Configuration Examples Configuration Guide The examples below are generic templates. Always refer to your specific LLM provider's official documentation for the most up-to-date configuration instructions, as setup details may vary between versions and providers. These examples use the US endpoint. If your workspace is EU hosted, replace https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp with https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp . See the connection URLs in How MCP Works . For OAuth authentication (recommended): { "mcpServers" : { "intercom" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "mcp-remote" , "https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp" ] } } } For Bearer token authentication : { "mcpServers" : { "intercom" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "mcp-remote" , "https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp" , "--header" , "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}" ], "env" : { "AUTH_HEADER" : "Bearer YOUR_INTERCOM_API_TOKEN" } } } } LLM Provider Setup Guides Each AI provider has specific setup instructions for MCP servers. Please consult the official documentation for your provider: Claude Desktop : MCP setup documentation Claude Code : MCP setup documentation OpenAI : MCP integration guide Claude.ai : The Intercom connector in Claude's directory connects to US hosted workspaces. For an EU hosted workspace, go to Customize > Connectors > + Add > Add custom connector and use https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp . On Claude Team or Enterprise, an org Owner adds it under Organization settings > Connectors. Cursor : MCP configuration guide Windsurf : MCP setup instructions VS Code : MCP integration docs Connecting your own MCP client The providers listed above are already on the allowlist. If you're building your own MCP client, OAuth client registration is automatic — the server supports Dynamic Client Registration — but every redirect URI a client registers is checked against an allowlist, which controls where the server will send authorization responses. What this means for your client: Bearer token authentication doesn't use a redirect URI, so there's nothing to request. OAuth with a callback on localhost or 127.0.0.1 is already allowed on any port, so you can develop and test locally right away. OAuth with any other callback needs an allowlist entry before the flow will complete. Until we've added your redirect URI, registration and authorization fail with one of these errors: Redirect URI https://your-app.example.com/callback is not in the allowlist, reach out to Intercom Customer Support if you believe we should support it Invalid request: Redirect URI is not allowed App Store review is a separate approval Submitting your app for review in the Developer Hub doesn't add its redirect URI to the MCP server allowlist, even though you register the URI there. If your app connects to the MCP server with OAuth, request an allowlist entry as well. Requesting an allowlist entry Contact Intercom Customer Support through the Messenger in the bottom right of this page, and include: The name of your client and what it does with Intercom data Each redirect URI in full, exactly as your client sends it The environment each URI serves: development, staging, or production Your workspace ID Whether you need a wildcard entry like https://*.example.com , and what it needs to cover We add the narrowest entry that covers your callbacks. For a host you own, that's usually the origin — an entry for https://app.example.com covers every path on that host. If your callback runs on a platform shared with other companies, we add the exact path instead, so list every path you use. Wildcards are granted only for domains where you control every subdomain. One entry covers both mcp.intercom.com and mcp.eu.intercom.com , so a single request is enough for both regions. Working with Pagination All search and list tools support pagination to handle large result sets efficiently. Cursor-based pagination is used by search , search_conversations , and search_contacts — use the starting_after parameter. Page-based pagination is used by list_articles , list_companies and list_audiences — use the page parameter. Example Pagination Workflow 1. Initial Search Request Using the search tool: object_type:conversations state:open limit:50 2. Response with More Results If more results exist, you'll receive: { "total_in_page" : 50 , "results" : [...], "pages" : { "type" : "pages" , "page" : 1 , "per_page" : 50 , "total_pages" : 5 , "next" : { "page" : 2 , "starting_after" : "cursor_abc123" } }, "_note" : "More results available. To get the next page, add to your query: starting_after:cursor_abc123" } 3. Fetch Next Page Use the cursor from the response: object_type:conversations state:open limit:50 starting_after:cursor_abc123 4. Continue Until Complete Keep paginating until the response no longer includes pages.next or _note , indicating you've reached the last page. Tool-Specific Pagination For search_conversations and search_contacts , use the starting_after parameter: { "state" : "open" , "per_page" : 50 , "starting_after" : "cursor_abc123" } The response will include the same pagination metadata to guide you through the result set. Required Scopes The Intercom MCP server requires the following permissions to access your workspace data. When using Bearer token authentication, ensure your access token includes these scopes. Learn more about OAuth permissions . Read and list users and companies : Required for contact and company data access Read conversations : Required for conversation data access Write conversations : Required for adding internal notes to conversations (add_internal_note) Read and write articles : Required for Help Center article access (list, search, get, create, update) Read audiences : Required for listing Fin audiences (list_audiences). An OAuth connection authorized before the Intercom MCP integration had this permission must be disconnected and reconnected to get it Read admins : Required for Bearer tokens on the tools that act as you: adding internal notes, creating and updating articles, and submitting feedback (add_internal_note, create_article, update_article, submit_mcp_feedback). OAuth connections need nothing extra for it Use Fin Operator : Required for the Fin Operator tools . Granted through OAuth only; it cannot be added to a Bearer token. During OAuth, the consent page summarizes these permissions as: view conversations and add internal notes to them, view contacts and companies, view, create and update articles, view Fin audiences, and use Fin Operator. The Use Fin Operator permission is requested for every connection, but the tools only work for workspaces that have Fin Operator. MCP Inspector for Server Exploration Test the connection using: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector Then connect to: Transport Type : Streamable HTTP URL : https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp (US) or https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp (EU), or /sse for legacy Debugging and Troubleshooting MCP-Remote Authentication Problems # Kill existing connections pkill -f mcp-remote # Clear MCP auth cache rm -rf ~/.mcp-auth Connection Testing # EU hosted workspaces: use https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp instead # Test direct connection npx mcp-remote https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp # With bearer token npx mcp-remote https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp --header "Authorization:Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" View Active MCP Connections ps aux | grep mcp-remote | grep -v grep Error Handling Invalid queries : The search tool validates field names and operators, returning specific error messages Authentication failures : Check token validity or restart OAuth flow Rate limiting : Intercom API limits apply - reduce request frequency if needed Troubleshooting Tips Restart AI Agent after configuration changes Use the MCP Inspector to verify tool availability Check browser console for OAuth-related errors Verify Intercom API token permissions for bearer auth The consent page expires after 15 minutes. If Allow shows "Authorization could not be completed", start the connection again from your client Only one connection can be pending per browser. Starting a second connection in another tab before finishing the first makes the first tab's Allow fail with the same message. Start the connection again An "Invalid redirect URI" error that says the URI does not match any registered URI for this client, shown before the consent page, means the client opened its callback on a port it did not register. Clear the client's saved authentication for the Intercom server (see Authentication Problems above) and connect again, so the client registers its current callback address The consent page only appears in the OAuth flow. Bearer token authentication is unchanged If you choose Allow and Intercom then shows "We're having technical difficulties", you most likely connected using another region's endpoint, for example the US endpoint for an EU hosted workspace. Remove the connection from your client and connect again using the endpoint for your workspace's region (see How MCP Works ). The MCP server isn't available for AU hosted workspaces. pages.title: Intercom developer FAQs | Intercom Help (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/9071694-intercom-developer-faqs)
pages.text: Intercom developer FAQs | Intercom Help Skip to main content Overview Getting Started Operator Fin AI Agent Channels Inbox Workflows Knowledge Reports Outbound Contacts Workforce Management Apps & Integrations Mobile SDKs Community Academy Security & Privacy Use this article to set up your Intercom developer environment, configure a custom Help Center domain with SSL, authenticate your app via access tokens or OAuth, and manage contacts, conversations, and tickets via the Intercom API (Application Programming Interface). It also covers webhooks, pagination, building Messenger and Inbox apps, and troubleshooting common API and SSL errors. Intended for developers building integrations with Intercom. Intercom developer documentation Intercom APIs Intercom SDKs Canvas Kit Webhooks Inbox Apps Messenger Apps Setting up Intercom How do I create a developer account? You can create a new developer workspace for developing apps. Developer workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only. Once you've created the new workspace you can follow this guide to create an app and make your first API call. You can create a new app for your production workspace and get the access token for the app by going to https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/{your-workspace-id}/developer-hub/ How do I set up a custom help center domain? When you turn on your Articles Help Center, your content is available through intercom.help by default. Your URL will look like this: intercom.help/exampleapp. If you'd like to use a different URL, you can create one by manually setting up a custom domain. This will involve entering the custom domain in your Help Center settings, creating a custom CNAME record, and optionally configuring SSL. Find the full instructions for set up in our developer documentation . If your Help Center shows a "not found" error after setting up a custom domain, verify your CNAME record to ensure your subdomain points to the correct Intercom host: • For HTTPS Quick Setup: us.intercomhelpcenter.com (US region) • For Manual/HTTP Setup: custom.intercom.help (US region) Also check that the security protocol selected in your Help Center settings matches your DNS setup. How do I set up SSL? SSL (or TLS), is the most widely used way to secure the connection between your server and your browser. It ensures the connection between the server and browser is encrypted and safe, and appears as HTTPS. There are two ways to set up SSL with Articles on your custom domain: Use a flexible SSL (using a third party DNS provider like CloudFlare or AWS CloudFront) Use your own SSL certificate (using a TLS Termination Proxy) Does Intercom handle SSL certificates for custom domains? Yes! If you enable “HTTPS (quick setup)” in your Help Center settings, Intercom will automatically provision and manage an SSL certificate for your custom domain (like https://help.ourdomain.com ). There's no need for a manual SSL setup — just point your CNAME to us.intercomhelpcenter.com, and we’ll handle the rest. Note : HTTPS (quick setup) isn't available by default for all workspaces - it's a setting our Support team can enable for you. Once enabled, the HTTPS (quick setup) option will appear in your Help Center settings. Follow the DNS setup instructions below to complete your configuration. How to enable HTTPS (quick setup) for your custom domain If you aim to switch your custom domain to HTTPS: Navigate to Settings > Help Center > Configure & Style . Head to the Domain section. Select HTTPS (quick setup) as your security protocol and save the changes. Upon activation, ensure your CNAME record points to [us.intercomhelpcenter.com]( https://us.intercomhelpcenter.com ) (or [eu.intercomhelpcenter.com]( https://eu.intercomhelpcenter.com ) for EU regions) via your domain provider. You should receive a confirmation email when the setup is successful, typically within 48 hours. You can configure SSL for your custom domain to keep sensitive information encrypted. If you want to do this, make sure you’ve set up your CNAME with a DNS provider that supports SSL, like Cloudflare. Follow the guide in our developer documentation for setting up SSL. Note that depending on the provider you have chosen set up steps may vary. Advanced troubleshooting If the standard SSL and HTTPS configuration steps haven't resolved your issue, the following scenarios cover common edge cases for custom Help Center domains: HTTPS Defaults to Manual Setup: Refer to our Custom Domains Guide for accurate configuration steps. Domain Displays as "Not Secure": To secure your help center hosted on HTTP, consider: Using a third-party DNS provider, such as Cloudflare or AWS CloudFront, for flexible SSL proxying. Employing a TLS Termination Proxy for advanced SSL certificate management. Common HTTPS/SSL issues and troubleshooting 1. Domain Not Secure Ensure only Intercom's SSL certificate is active for your domain. Remove or disable any additional certificates from your host or CDN (Content Delivery Network). If using a CDN such as Cloudflare, set the proxy status to "DNS only" (grey cloud icon). Verify your DNS CNAME record points to the correct Intercom endpoint (us.intercomhelpcenter.com for US, eu.intercomhelpcenter.com for EU). ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH Error Verify that your CNAME (Canonical Name) record points to [us.intercomhelpcenter.com]( https://us.intercomhelpcenter.com ) . Confirm that no conflicting DNS (Domain Name System) records exist. Only one CNAME should be active for the domain entry. Delete any duplicates. Ensure DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours, has been completed. You can use tools like whatsmydns.net to check global propagation. 2. HTTPS Setup Stuck on Pending Check for common DNS configuration issues, such as formatting errors in the CNAME record (for example, accidentally appending .yourdomain.com ) or using an incorrect record type (for example, an A record instead of CNAME). Ensure the CNAME record points to us.intercomhelpcenter.com (or eu.intercomhelpcenter.com for EU regions). After corrections, wait for DNS propagation, which can take up to 72 hours. Use whatsmydns.net to verify global propagation before testing again. 3. HTTPS (Quick Setup) Option Not Available Contact Fin Support to have HTTPS quick setup enabled for your workspace — it isn't available by default. Ensure your domain is not already in use by another Intercom account. Verify that a CNAME record has been added to your DNS provider, pointing to us.intercomhelpcenter.com . 4. Access Denied Error Verify the CNAME record points correctly to us.intercomhelpcenter.com . If using Cloudflare, set SSL to 'Flexible' or 'Full' — avoid 'Full (Strict)'. Toggle the SSL configuration off and back on to restart the SSL provisioning sequence. Help Center URL and domain management Broken URLs after migration If a migrated article URL no longer works after moving content to Intercom: Create a new public article to replace the broken URL. Update any calls to action or links in your content to point to the new article's URL. "Not found" error when articles look fine internally If your Help Center shows a "Not found" error on the public URL but articles appear correctly in your workspace: Check whether your Help Center is set to Live in your settings. Navigate to Settings > Help Center and set the status to Live to make the public URL accessible. The Intercom API What is the current version of the API? The current version of the API is 2.18. You can find the documentation for the API on our developer documentation site . You can also change the version that your app is using in your Developer Hub by following the steps listed in this guide . If you are using the Intercom API, you can also change the version within the HTTP header of your request. Note: The developer documentation also keeps reference pages for the legacy 1.x API (URLs containing /docs/references/1.0/ or /docs/references/1.1/ ). Those pages describe endpoints such as /users and /leads that aren't used in version 2.x. Make sure you're following the current version's reference pages under /docs/references/rest-api/ . What endpoints are available in the current version of the API? Key endpoints available in version 2.18 of the Intercom API include the ones below. Newer APIs, such as Folders, Dynamic Content, Roles, Auth Tokens, and Granted Companies, are also available in 2.18. For the full list, see the API reference . Admins Articles Companies Contacts Conversations Data Attributes Data Events Data Export Help Center Messages News Notes Segments Subscription Types Switch Tags Teams Ticket Type Attributes Ticket Types Tickets Visitors Models Can I trigger an article to open in the Messenger from a button? Yes, if you'd like to trigger an article in the Messenger, you can use the showArticle method from the JavaScript API. The article will open within the Messenger and clicking the Messenger back button will return to the previous context. If the Messenger is closed when the method is called, it will be opened first and then the article will be shown. This is available across all platforms in the Messenger. How to trigger an article from HTML # You can add a link anywhere on your site to open an article in the Messenger: Open article Contacts Should I use the /users or /contacts endpoint? Use /contacts . In the current API, users and leads are both contacts, and you create or update them with the Create a contact ( POST /contacts ) and Update a contact ( PUT /contacts/{id} ) endpoints. POST /users is a legacy 1.x endpoint and won't work with current API versions. How do I create a contact without an email address? A contact needs at least an email or an external_id . To create a user without an email, send your own unique identifier for them as external_id . In the /contacts endpoints this field is called external_id , not user_id . Sending user_id without an email returns the error either_email_or_user_id_present validation failed . POST https://api.intercom.io/contacts { "external_id": "cust_001", "name": "Jane Doe", "custom_attributes": { "Currency": "EUR" } } Any custom attributes you set must already exist in Settings > Data > People , otherwise the request returns an error saying the attribute doesn't exist. Can I bulk create users using the API? Yes. In Intercom users fall under the label of contacts. You can use the Bulk create contacts endpoint to create many contacts in one request. Alternatively, you can use the create contact endpoint in a script that imports users one at a time, or follow this tutorial for code samples to get started. Be sure to set up a rate limiting check to make sure you are not hitting the limit, See What are the current rate limits? below for the limits that apply to public and private apps. Bulk operations and their limitations To import contacts at scale, use the Bulk create contacts endpoint , or the create contact endpoint in a loop with appropriate rate-limit handling. Ensure your script respects the rate limits . The following bulk operations are not available via the API and must be handled through looped single-item requests or manual export/import: Bulk conversation export (use the Data Export endpoint for conversation data exports) Bulk note deletion (notes must be deleted one at a time from the workspace UI) How can I retrieve an archived user's data? To retrieve an archived contact's data you first need to unarchive the contact, which you can do with the unarchive contact API endpoint if you have the contact's ID. Then you will be able to regain access to the contacts data through the get a contact API endpoint and their conversations through the retrieve a conversation API endpoint . It's not possible to unarchive a user or contact from the UI, it has to be done through the API. Can I delete notes on my contacts via the API? No, there is currently no way to delete individual notes or bulk delete notes from contacts via the API. If this functionality is important for your operations, please visit the Product Wishlist to create, comment on, or upvote a feature request. Notes can be deleted manually within the workspace, but only one at a time. Conversations How do I assign conversations to a team using the API? If you would like to assign a conversation to a team using the API you have two options. The first option is to assign a conversation directly to an admin or a team using the manage a conversation API endpoint . You need to have access to the Intercom provisioned id for the conversation as well as the admin_id and the assignee_id. The other option is to run assignment rules that you have already set up on the conversation using the run assignment rules on a conversation API endpoint . You need to have access to the Intercom provisioned id for the conversation. You can test out the functionality from the "Try It" feature in our developer documentation , the Intercom Postman collection , or in your own terminal or IDE (Integrated Development Environment). Don't forget to use your Intercom access token as a bearer token. How do I add notes to conversations via the API? A note in an internal comment only visible to teammates. To add a note to a conversation you can use the reply to a conversation API endpoint . You will need to choose a messsage_type of note and a type of "admin" along with the admin_id that the note should come from. You can test out the functionality from the "Try It" feature in our developer documentation , the Intercom Postman collection , or in your own terminal or IDE. Don't forget to use your Intercom access token as a bearer token. How do I add tags to conversations via the API? If you have already created a tag in the UI, you can use that tag to apply to conversations. You can also create a new tag using the API. To use the add tag to a conversation API endpoint , you will need to have access to the conversation_id of the conversation to tag, the Intercom provisioned id of the tag and the admin_id. You can test out the functionality from the "Try It" feature in our developer documentation , the Intercom Postman collection , or in your own terminal or IDE. Don't forget to use your Intercom access token as a bearer token. How do I create a conversation using the API? You can create a conversation from the API that has been initiated by a contact (ie. user or lead) by using the create a conversation API endpoint . The conversation can be an in-app message only. You will also need the Intercom provisioned id for the contact and the body text to use as the message body when making the request. You can test out the functionality from the "Try It" feature in our developer documentation , the Intercom Postman collection , or in your own terminal or IDE. Don't forget to use your Intercom access token as a bearer token. By default, a conversation created this way won't appear in the Inbox — and won't be searchable via Conversation search — until the contact replies to it. To make the conversation appear in the Inbox immediately, without waiting for the contact to reply, include "create_conversation_without_contact_reply": true in the request payload. This defaults to false if not provided. What if the conversation doesn't appear at all, even with an ID? If the request payload's body field is missing, empty, or malformed, the API can still return a success response and create a conversation shell with no message content attached. Because the Inbox can't render a conversation with no messages, opening it in the UI returns a 404 ("Could not load conversation"), even though the conversation can still be retrieved via the API by ID. If this happens, check that the integration's body field is present and non-empty, and that message_type is set correctly (e.g. inapp or email). An existing broken conversation of this kind can't be recovered — it must be recreated with a corrected payload. How do I delete conversations with the API? To close a conversation using the API you can use the manage a conversation API endpoint . You will need to have the Intercom provisioned id of the conversation, your admin_id and use a message_type of "close". If you need to redact only a certain part of the conversation, use the redact a conversation part API endpoint . You can test out the functionality from the "Try It" feature in our developer documentation , the Intercom Postman collection , or in your own terminal or IDE. Don't forget to use your Intercom access token as a bearer token. How can I set up custom notifications for when a teammate is assigned to a conversation? To set up a custom notification when an action is taken, such as a teammate being assigned to a conversation, you can use webhooks . You will want to use the conversation.admin.assigned conversation topic. You can find all of the conversation topics in our developer documentation . You can then subscribe to this webhook topic in the developer hub by following the steps in this guide . You'll also need to have a publicly accessible endpoint URL available for the action to take once the webhook is hit to deliver the notification to your channel of choice. How do I access side conversations via the API? Side conversations don't have their own dedicated endpoint, so you can’t retrieve them directly. However, when you retrieve a conversation that the side conversation is attached to, you will see conversation parts that show as "part_type": "side_conversation_reply" with the content of the user's messages in the side conversation. Tickets How do I create a ticket using the API? To create a ticket using the Intercom API, you will first need to create or obtain the type of ticket to label the new ticket. Then you can create the ticket using a curl request or with a programming language of your choice. Follow this guide from our developer documentation to create a ticket type and create a new ticket. How can I flag back office tickets so they aren't counted when using the API? If you are using the API to retrieve tickets and ticket data, you can use the search tickets API endpoint . To exclude back office ticket types, set the field to ticket_type_id and use the != operator to exclude the ticket_type_id assigned to back office ticket types. If you are using the API to retrieve a conversation or list conversations with back office tickets associated with the conversations and you'd like to exclude them, you can similarly filter out any results that have the back office ticket type as an attribute. Linked tickets can be found at the tickets parameter in the response or under linked_objects. One other option available is to use the API to tag conversations with a back office ticket associated with them. You can then use the tag in order to filter by ticket category. Error Codes and Messages What does a 403 API Plan restricted error message in a response mean? If you are getting a 403 API Plan restricted message in a response this means that the API you are trying to use is not available on your app's plan. In order to access the API you'll need to upgrade your plan. You can find out more about Intercom plans on this page . You can find a full list of error codes and HTTP responses in our developer documentation. What does a 409 conflict error message in a response mean? If you are getting a 409 conflict message in a response this means there is existing data in your Intercom workspace that clashes with the request data. This can occur if you try to create a contact and there is a contact with that email address already added within your app. To avoid this error you can use the update endpoint instead or create a new contact by external_id. You can find a full list of error codes and HTTP responses in our developer documentation. What does a 429 error message in a response mean? If you are getting a 429 message it means the client has reached or exceeded a rate limit, or the server is overloaded. See What are the current rate limits? for the default limits for public and private apps. More information on rate limits is available in our developer documentation . To avoid this error you can set up a rate limiting check to make sure you are not hitting the limit. You can find a full list of error codes and HTTP responses in our developer documentation. What are the current rate limits? Private apps have a default rate limit of 10,000 API calls per minute per workspace, shared by all private apps in the workspace. This means that if a workspace has multiple private apps installed, every one contributes towards the same total. Public apps have a default rate limit of 10,000 API calls per minute for each app and 25,000 API calls per minute per workspace. This means that if a workspace has multiple public apps installed, each one has its own separate request limit without contributing to the others. More information on rate limits is available in our developer documentation . Reporting Why is my report different when pulled from the API vs UI? If you are creating your own reports using the API you may notice that there are some differences between the two reports. This can happen for a few reasons. One common issue is when dates and times do not match. This is often because the time zone that you are using in your Intercom workspace is different than the time zone you are using to query the API. To fix this, either adjust your API query parameters to match your workspace time zone, or change the time zone of your custom report. Another issue is that you may be using metrics that do not align with the Intercom reporting UI metrics. There are some metrics available in the reporting UI that are not available via the API because they are calculated metrics. Some of those can be created by using the API and performing the calculations on your end. Check out the guide for building your own reports from the Intercom developer documentation. Are back office tickets counted in the statistics when pulling a report from API? If you are looking at the conversations reports available in the UI versus reports pulled using the conversations API, you may notice that there is a difference in the number of conversations. This is because back office tickets associated with a conversation will be included when it is pulled from the API. To solve for this, you can filter results after retrieving them via the list conversations , retrieve a conversation , or search for conversations API, and separate the tickets from conversations using the ticket field in the conversation API response. The ticket field will be populated with an object if it is a ticket and will be null if it is a conversation. Webhooks What webhooks are available? Webhooks allow you to subscribe to real-time notifications of events happening in Intercom, like when a contact is created or an incoming message is received. You can see the webhooks available for each version in our developer documentation . Once you've identified which webhook you need follow this guide to set them up. Are there plans to add new webhooks? There are no plans to add new webhooks on our roadmap, but if there is a webhook your team needs, please submit a request to the team or add it to the product wishlist in the Intercom community. Webhook reliability and delivery When building on Intercom webhooks, keep the following in mind: Retry policy: Intercom retries failed webhook deliveries. If your endpoint returns a non-2xx response, Intercom will retry the request. Design your endpoint to handle duplicate deliveries (make it idempotent). Timeout: Your endpoint must respond within a short window. If it times out, the delivery is treated as a failure and retried. Ordering: Webhook events are not guaranteed to arrive in the exact order they occurred. Use event timestamps to sequence events correctly in your system. Debugging: The Developer Hub doesn't show a history of webhook deliveries or the payloads that were sent. To debug missed or malformed events, log incoming requests on your own endpoint, including the topic, notification ID and response code you return. In the Developer Hub, under your app's webhook settings, you can preview an example payload for each topic, and saving your webhook settings sends a test request to your endpoint URL to confirm it can receive notifications. If you need help investigating specific deliveries, contact Fin Support. Pagination How does pagination work? Intercom APIs for listing and searching resources offer cursor-based pagination. This is available so that when you are requesting a large amount of data — like many conversations with all of their parts — you can receive and process them in smaller chunks. For examples on how to use pagination with both the Intercom list APIs, which accept path parameters, and search APIs, which use query parameters, see our pagination guide . How do I used the starting_after field? For cursor-based pagination, Intercom uses a pointer that will refer to a specific record based on the limit that you set by the number of pages that you specify per request. When returned in an object, the pointer will look something like 'WzXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'. You can then use the pointer from the response in order to make the subsequent request for the next batch of data. The pagination formatting in the request differs slightly between list APIs and search APIs, but the responses work the same. You can see examples of curl requests on our Pagination page , and tutorials on using list API s, and search APIs . Authentication What type of authentication is required for public apps? Any apps that interact with third party workspace data and apps built with Canvas Kit require OAuth to be in place. You should never ask users for their access token and only use OAuth for interacting with their data. See the documentation for instructions on setting up OAuth . Do I have to use OAuth for my app? You'll need to set up OAuth if you're building an integration with Intercom that accesses other peoples' Intercom data. This includes public apps that you plan to list on the Intercom app store as well as apps and integrations you will ask users to install through your own website. Learn more about OAuth from our developer documentation . If you are only accessing data within you own Intercom workspace you can use an access token . What type of authentication is required for private apps? If you're building a private app that only accesses data in your Intercom workspace, you can use your Intercom access token for authentication. Find your access token in your developer hub and learn more about authentication here . Where can I find my Intercom access token? You can use your Intercom access token if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace. Find your access token in your developer hub and learn more about authentication here . To find your API access token, follow these steps: Open the Intercom Developer Hub . Navigate to Your Apps at Developer Hub > Settings > Your Apps. You should see a list of apps associated with your workspace. Locate your private app, which may include your workspace’s name and sometimes the suffix "Access Token App." Click the app name to open its details. Go to the Authentication section to find the token. Treat this token like a password, as it is private and should not be shared. Can I rotate or change my OAuth Client Secret? You can't rotate your app's OAuth Client Secret yourself, but our support team can rotate it for you on request. Once it's rotated, the old secret stops working immediately and the new secret is available in the Developer Hub. Important: The old secret is invalidated immediately upon rotation. Be ready to update your integration's configuration as soon as the rotation takes place to avoid any service interruption. To request a rotation, message us in the Messenger and ask to speak to the support team. Include your app's name and Client ID, and agree on a time for the rotation so your team can update your integration's configuration with the new secret straight away. Installing and Publishing Apps How do I build an app for my Inbox? You can build an app for your Intercom Inbox by using Canvas Kit, a toolkit that allows you to build apps that work from directly within the Intercom UI. Follow this tutorial to learn how to build your first Inbox app. You can also learn more about Canvas Kit and find reference docs in our developer documentation . How do I build an app for my Messenger? You can build an app for your Intercom Messenger by using Canvas Kit, a toolkit that allows you to build apps that work from directly within the Intercom UI. Note that customizations are limited to what is capable through Canvas Kit and must be created within the Messenger: it's not possible to recreate or re-skin the Messenger. Follow this tutorial to learn how to build your first Inbox app. You can also learn more about Canvas Kit and find reference docs in our developer documentation . How do I install my app? If you visit the Test & Publish > Your Workspaces page of your app in the Developer Hub then you should see all the workspaces you (as an Intercom teammate) are a member of. You can click on Install app next to the workspace you want to install the given app on. This app will then be installed and an Access Token will be provided for that workspace so you can access its data through the API. For third-party installation instructions, see our developer documentation . How can I publish my app to the Intercom app store? When you are ready to publish your app, you can follow the steps in the developer hub. You can find a guide on how to publish your app in our developer documentation . Messenger How do I install the Messenger for iOS? The Intercom SDK (Software Development Kit) for iOS enables you to use the Intercom Messenger in your app, have conversations with your customers, send rich outbound messages, show your Help Center, and track events. You can install Intercom for iOS using Cocoapods, Swift Package Manager, or manually. Read the full iOS installation guide . You can find Intercom for iOS on GitHub along with a sample app to explore the SDK. How do I install the Messenger for Android? The Intercom SDK for Android enables you to use the Intercom Messenger in your app, have conversations with your customers, send rich outbound messages, show your Help Center, and track events. You can install Intercom for Android using Gradle or manually. Read the full Android installation guide . You can find Intercom for Android on GitHub along with a sample app to explore the SDK. How do I install the Messenger for React Native? The Intercom React Native wrapper allows you to use Intercom for iOS and Intercom for Android in your React Native apps. Follow the React Native installation guide to get started. 💡 Tip Need more help? Get support from our Community Forum Find answers and get help from Intercom Support and Community Experts Did this answer your question? pages.title: Add MCP connectors for popular apps or custom MCPs | Intercom Help (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/11461635-add-mcp-connectors-for-popular-apps-or-custom-mcps)
pages.text: Add MCP connectors for popular apps or custom MCPs | Intercom Help Skip to main content Overview Getting Started Operator Fin AI Agent Channels Inbox Workflows Knowledge Reports Outbound Contacts Workforce Management Apps & Integrations Mobile SDKs Community Academy Security & Privacy Fin can now connect directly to your other business tools, like project management (Linear) or billing systems (Stripe), using a new feature called MCP connectors (Model Context Protocol) . This allows Fin to access real-time information and even perform actions in those external systems, leading to more complete and efficient resolutions for your customers. Note : For tools like Linear, app attributes cannot be used in Intercom reporting. A workaround is to create custom attributes in Intercom and use them as a column in reports. What are MCP connectors? MCP connectors are a powerful way for Fin to interact with your external applications and data sources. Think of it as giving Fin a secure key to access specific information and capabilities from other software you use. Instead of Fin only knowing what's in Intercom or your Help Center, it can now tap into data like: Stripe — The MCP integration for Fin imports Stripe connectors for billing and subscription management. Shopify — The Shopify Storefront MCP tools were retired on August 31, 2026. To connect a Shopify store, use the Shopify GraphQL Storefront templates instead. See Migrate your Shopify Storefront MCP connectors . Linear — The MCP integration for Fin imports Linear connectors for issue and project management. Zapier — The Zapier template is currently paused and not generally available. You can use the Custom MCP option to connect Zapier in the meantime. See Connect the Zapier MCP connector to Fin . This makes Fin much smarter and more capable of handling complex customer queries without needing to hand off to a teammate. Key benefits of using MCP connectors Access More Data: Fin gets real-time access to information from your connected systems. Automate More Actions: Enable Fin to take actions in external tools (e.g., create a ticket, update a status) if the tool supports it. Faster, More Accurate Resolutions: Customers get the answers they need more quickly, directly from Fin. Reduced Agent Handoffs: Fin can handle more queries independently, freeing up your team. Easy, Secure Setup: Connect your tools in a few steps using industry-standard authentication. Setting up MCP connectors for Fin Once enabled for your workspace, you'll find the MCP settings within Settings > Integrations > Data connectors . Connecting an MCP server You can connect an MCP server in two ways: 1. Connect using a template For popular applications, we provide pre-built templates for a quicker setup, including Stripe and Linear. The Zapier template is currently paused, and the Shopify Storefront MCP template was retired on August 31, 2026. Navigate to Settings > Integrations > Data connectors . You'll see a section titled "Add Data Connectors from popular apps — powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers." Click on the tile for the app you want to connect (e.g., Linear ). Note: The app must be installed on your workspace to use a Data connector template. Authorize access to the MCP Server If the third party MCP server supports OAuth you will be redirected to the application's website to authorize Intercom Fin to access your data. Follow the on-screen prompts (this typically involves an OAuth flow). Otherwise an access token can be created or an existing one chosen from the Authentication Settings page in Intercom. Once authorized, you'll be redirected back to Intercom. The connected MCP server will now appear in your list of data connectors, usually with "(0)" indicating no tools have been added yet (e.g., "Linear (0)") 2. Connect a Custom MCP server If you have your own MCP server or are connecting a third-party service that doesn't have a template yet: Navigate to Settings > Integrations > Data connectors . Click on the Custom MCP tile. ​ A modal will appear where you'll need to enter: Name: A descriptive name for this connection (e.g., "Our Internal CRM," "Linear Dev"). URL: The base URL of the MCP server (e.g., https://mcp.your-service.com/sse ). You'll get this URL from your MCP server provider. You can choose to provide an access token if your chosen server supports token based authentication, if none is provided we will attempt to initiate and OAuth flow with the provided MCP server Click Add MCP Server. Once authorized, the custom MCP server will be listed in your data connectors. Adding tools from a connected MCP server Once an MCP server is connected, you need to tell Fin which specific "tools" (functions or data points) from that server it can use. Find your newly connected MCP server in the list (e.g., "Linear (0)"). Click the "+ New" button located under that server's section. A modal will appear (e.g., "Linear Connectors") listing all the available tools provided by that MCP server (e.g., "List Comments," "Create Issue," "Get Order Details"). Click on the tool you want Fin to use (e.g., "List Comments"). The tool will now be added as a Data connector under that MCP server's section. The count next to the server name will update (e.g., "Linear (1)"). Configuring an MCP tool (Data connector) Each tool added from an MCP server acts like a standard Data connector and needs to be configured before Fin can use it. Click on the newly added tool (e.g., "List comments") to open its configuration page. You'll see the same tabs as a standard data connector: API , Data , Fin , and Security . A. API tab — name and description: Name & Description: These are usually pre-filled from the MCP server. You can edit them if needed. How should Fin use this connector? (on the Fin tab): Choose Enabled (direct trigger) if you want Fin to decide when to use this tool based on the conversation, using its name and description. Choose Disabled (manual trigger) to add it to a Fin Workflow or Procedure instead. Audience (on the Fin tab): Define who this connector is available for (e.g., Users, Leads). B. API tab — input parameters: This tab shows the inputs the tool requires (e.g., an "IssueID" for a "List Comments" tool). For each input, you need to specify the Data Source : Let Fin decide: Fin will try to find the information from the conversation, previous actions, or ask the customer. Set a custom value: Hardcode a specific value. Use an attribute: Pull the value from an Intercom user, company, or conversation attribute. Ignore Input: Optional parameters can be ignored and will not be included in the request C. API tab — test the tool: Test the tool to ensure it's working correctly. Live response: Makes an actual API call to the MCP server. Example response: Provide sample JSON data to simulate a response. D. Data tab: Note: We highly recommend exercising extreme caution with what tools are made available to Fin. Any data that is returned to Fin from a tool response may be shared with the customer. Configure this tab just like you would for standard API-based data connectors. Here you can define how Fin interprets and uses the data returned by the tool. Refer to our general data connector documentation for details. E. Security tab and set live: Review the security checks on the Security tab, then click the Set live button at the top of the page. The tool's status will change from "Draft" to "Live," and Fin will now be able to use it. ​ Note: Fin can only process one connector call per turn, so if your MCP server sends back two separate responses over the same SSE stream, Fin will not be able to reliably use the first response to build its answer. How Fin uses MCP tools Once an MCP tool is live: If the connector is set to Enabled (direct trigger): Fin will analyze customer conversations. If it determines that the tool can help resolve the query (based on the tool's name and description, and the inputs it requires), Fin will automatically try to collect the necessary inputs and use the tool. If not enabled for direct use, or for more complex scenarios: You can add these MCP tools as steps within your Fin Workflows and Procedures , giving you precise control over when and how they are used. Fin makes a request to the MCP server, gets a response, and uses the information (based on your object mapping) to answer the customer or perform further actions. Supported apps and custom connections Templates: Templates are available for Linear and Stripe . The Zapier template is currently paused and not generally available — use the Custom MCP option to connect Zapier in the meantime. The Shopify Storefront MCP template was retired on August 31, 2026; use the Shopify GraphQL Storefront templates instead. Custom MCP: You can connect to any system that provides an MCP-compliant server using the "Custom MCP" option. You will need the MCP server URL from the provider of that system and authentication details depending on the supported authentication types (OAuth or Token based). Security Connecting Fin to external systems is done securely: OAuth 2.0: Connections to third-party MCP servers are authenticated using OAuth 2.0 , an industry-standard protocol for authorization. Granular Permissions: During the OAuth process, you grant Intercom Fin specific permissions to access data or perform actions. You are in control of what Fin can access. Token Based Access: Where supported, a third party access token can be stored securely in Intercom and used to authenticate with the MCP server Note: MCP doesn't currently support all the same token types as standard data connectors. MCP has its own specific auth flow. FAQs What is Model Context Protocol (MCP)? It's a standardized way for AI models like Fin to discover and interact with external tools and data sources. Is connecting to MCP servers secure? Yes, connections use either OAuth 2.0 (an industry-standard for secure authorization), or token based access. What if the app I want to connect isn't listed as a template? If the app or system provides an MCP server, you can connect it using the "Custom MCP" option by providing its MCP server URL and authentication details. Where do I get the MCP Server URL for a custom connection? You'll need to get this URL from the documentation or support team of the application or system you are trying to connect. Does Intercom have a hosted MCP server that I can connect to an AI tool? Yes, Intercom has a hosted MCP server that you can connect to an MCP-compatible AI tool, so the tool can access your Intercom data, such as conversations, contacts, companies, and Help Center articles. The Intercom MCP server works in the opposite direction from MCP connectors. With MCP connectors, Fin connects to your external MCP servers. With the Intercom MCP server, an AI tool connects to your Intercom workspace. Operator's tools are included in the Intercom MCP server, so anyone entitled to use Operator can use it from Claude, Claude Code, or any other MCP client that supports OAuth. Operator actions taken this way use Operator credits as normal. The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces. AU hosted workspaces are not yet supported. How do I connect an AI tool to the Intercom MCP server for a US or EU hosted workspace? To connect an AI tool to the Intercom MCP server, use the server URL that matches your workspace's hosted region. A workspace URL of app.intercom.com means US hosted, and app.eu.intercom.com means EU hosted. US hosted workspaces: Connect your MCP client to https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp . EU hosted workspaces: Connect your MCP client to https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp . After you add the connection, your MCP client opens an OAuth (Open Authorization) sign-in. The Intercom MCP consent page names the application asking to connect and lists what it can do in your workspace. Check that the Redirects to address belongs to the application you expect, then click Allow. If Intercom shows "We're having technical difficulties" after you click Allow, you most likely connected with the wrong region's URL. Remove the connection and connect again with the URL for your workspace's region. For the full setup guide, see the Intercom Developer Docs: Model Context Protocol (MCP) . ​ 💡 Tip Need more help?
